plan.notes: Source: official Colorado State University General Catalog page 'Major in Computer Science, Computer Science Concentration' (College of Natural Sciences), https://catalog.colostate.edu/general-catalog/colleges/natural-sciences/computer-science/computer-science-major/computer-science-concentration/ The CSU catalog homepage states the General Catalog is re-published every August; the live catalog references the 2026-2027 academic year (estimated 2026-2027 expenses, Spring 2027 class schedule, experimental courses 2026-27), so the recorded catalog year is 2026-2027. The concentration page itself is marked 'Effective Fall 2025' (the program's effective term). Transcribed by hand on 2026-09-30 from the catalog's 'Major Completion Map' (Semesters 1-8, program total 120 credits). Credential honesty: CSU requires every Computer Science major to select a concentration; this plan follows the general Computer Science concentration (the broad, non-specialized option, 'prepares students for any introductory position in the computer science field'), and the degree awarded is the Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (per CSU's College of Natural Sciences). All course codes, titles, and credit hours are verbatim from the official map. Caveats: (1) several map rows are student-choice credit ranges; elective/choice-row credits were fixed within the catalog's printed ranges so each semester total matches the map and the program totals exactly 120 (Fall Y2: 15 of 14-16; Spring Y2: 15 of 14-16; Fall Y3: 15 of 14-15; Spring Y3: 15 of 15-16). (2) Student-choice slots use choice:true with descriptive codes; 'options' lists the catalog's named alternatives. (3) The catalog does not publish per-slot prerequisites in the completion map, so prereq arrays are intentionally left empty - consult the official catalog course pages and an academic advisor. (4) Map footnotes preserved: MATH 124/126 may be necessary for students needing pre-calculus; CO 150 must be completed by the end of Semester 2 with a grade of C or better; CS 165 and CS 220 must be completed by the end of Semester 4; MATH 156 or MATH 160, and MATH 369 or DSCI 369, must be completed by the end of Semester 4; CS 253 and (CS 250 or CS 270) must be completed by the end of Semester 5; CS 314, CS 320, and CS 370 must be completed by the end of Semester 6; at least 2 upper-division CS classes must be completed by the end of Semester 7; a C (2.000) or better is required in CO 150 and in all CS, DSCI, MATH, STAT, and departmental Technology Focus Elective courses.

courses.title: Culture and Coding: Python (GT-AH3) - recommended Group A intro course
courses.choice_note: First course from Group A, B, or C (AUCC 3B, 3 credits; recommended slot). Recommended sequence for most incoming students is Group A: CS 150B to CS 164. Group A: CS 150A or CS 150B (Culture and Coding: Java / Python, GT-AH3) then CS 162 or CS 164. Group B: CS 152 (Python for STEM), CS 162 or CS 164, plus an Arts and Humanities (3B) course. Group C: CS 163 (CS1-No Prior Programming Experience) plus an Arts and Humanities (3B) course. The Group A first course (CS 150B) is shown.
